# 1. Load & Prepare Data

Two changes versus the original `load_cs()`:

1. **Contiguous integer period index.** The original coded `period` as
   `YYYY*100 + MM` (e.g. 202012, 202101). `aggte(type = "dynamic")` computes
   event time as `e = t - g` from the *raw* `tname`/`gname` values, so across a
   year boundary that difference is 89, not 1. The `type = "simple"`
   aggregation that feeds the headline table is unaffected (it only needs the
   post/pre ordering), but the dynamic event-study plots and the
   `min_e`/`max_e` windows are distorted. Coding `period` as a dense rank
   (1, 2, 3, ...) makes both aggregations correct regardless of `did` version.

2. **Quarterly aggregation.** When `TIME_UNIT == "quarter"`, raw monthly
   counts are summed within firm-quarter *before* the `log1p`, and `g` is
   floored to the quarter that contains the approval date. Aggregating the
   counts and then logging (rather than averaging monthly logs) is the
   correct order for an additive count outcome.

```{r time-helpers}
# Floor a Date to the start of its time unit
floor_unit <- function(d, unit = TIME_UNIT) {
  if (unit == "month") {
    as.Date(format(d, "%Y-%m-01"))
  } else {  # quarter
    q  <- (as.integer(format(d, "%m")) - 1L) %/% 3L          # 0..3
    mm <- sprintf("%02d", q * 3L + 1L)                       # 01,04,07,10
    as.Date(paste0(format(d, "%Y"), "-", mm, "-01"))
  }
}

# All n_collabs* columns are outcome counts; everything else is meta/covariate
count_cols <- function(df) grep("^n_collabs", names(df), value = TRUE)
```

```{r load-data}
load_cs <- function(path, unit = TIME_UNIT) {
  df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df$month <- as.Date(df$month)

  ccols <- count_cols(df)

  # Covariates that are constant within firm (carried through aggregation)
  firm_cov <- c("g", "is_treated", "is_control", "matched_to",
                "nace1_psm", "nace1_proxy", "firm_type",
                "log_staffCount", "age",
                "log_collab_count_2020", "degree_centrality_2020")
  firm_cov <- intersect(firm_cov, names(df))

  # ── Collapse to the chosen time unit ───────────────────────────────────────
  df$tunit <- floor_unit(df$month, unit)

  # Level outcomes (per-month means, e.g. consortium size) are AVERAGED within
  # firm-quarter, NOT summed like the counts. (Absent in old panels -> no-op.)
  level_cols <- intersect(c("mean_collab_size", "mean_collab_size_active"), names(df))

  if (unit == "quarter") {
    counts <- df %>%
      group_by(Linkedin_name, tunit) %>%
      summarise(across(all_of(ccols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                .groups = "drop")
    meta <- df %>%
      group_by(Linkedin_name) %>%
      summarise(across(all_of(firm_cov), ~ dplyr::first(.x)),
                .groups = "drop")
    levels_q <- if (length(level_cols)) df %>%
      group_by(Linkedin_name, tunit) %>%
      summarise(across(all_of(level_cols), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),  # AVERAGE, not sum
                .groups = "drop") else NULL
    df <- counts %>% left_join(meta, by = "Linkedin_name")
    if (!is.null(levels_q)) df <- df %>% left_join(levels_q, by = c("Linkedin_name", "tunit"))
  } else {
    # monthly: tunit == month, nothing to sum, just keep one row per firm-month
    # (.keep_all carries mean_collab_size through unchanged)
    df <- df %>% distinct(Linkedin_name, tunit, .keep_all = TRUE)
  }

  # ── Contiguous integer period index (1..T) ─────────────────────────────────
  u_periods   <- sort(unique(df$tunit))
  period_idx  <- setNames(seq_along(u_periods), as.character(u_periods))
  df$period   <- as.integer(period_idx[as.character(df$tunit)])

  # ── g_period on the same contiguous scale (0 = never-treated) ───────────────
  df$g <- as.character(df$g)
  df$g[df$g == "" | df$g == "NA"] <- NA
  g_unit <- floor_unit(as.Date(df$g), unit)
  df$g_period <- period_idx[as.character(g_unit)]
  df$g_period[is.na(df$g_period)] <- 0L
  df$g_period <- as.numeric(df$g_period)

  df$firm_id <- as.integer(factor(df$Linkedin_name))

  # ── log1p every count column generically -> log_<name> ─────────────────────
  for (cc in ccols) {
    df[[sub("^n_collabs", "log_collabs", cc)]] <- log1p(df[[cc]])
  }

  # ── extensive-margin (binary) version of every count column ────────────────
  for (cc in ccols) {
    df[[sub("^n_collabs", "any_collabs", cc)]] <- as.integer(df[[cc]] > 0)
  }

  # ── difference-of-logs contrasts (mirrors _cs_helpers.R::load_cs) ──────────
  # Built here so the inline PSM loader and the shared helper stay identical.
  # They are NOT added to outcome_map below, so they never enter att_table or
  # its Benjamini-Hochberg family; they are estimated as secondary analyses in
  # 10_ck_diagnostics_reference_country.R and reported with nominal p-values.
  for (tech in c("battery", "hydrogen")) {
    f <- paste0("log_collabs_", tech)
    u <- paste0("log_collabs_nonfunded_", tech)
    if (all(c(f, u) %in% names(df)))
      df[[paste0("log_rel_tech_", tech)]] <- df[[f]] - df[[u]]
    e <- paste0("log_collabs_eu_crossborder_", tech)
    n <- paste0("log_collabs_non_eu_", tech)
    if (all(c(e, n) %in% names(df)))
      df[[paste0("log_rel_geo_", tech)]] <- df[[e]] - df[[n]]
  }

  df
}

battery_s1  <- load_cs(PATH_BATTERY_S1)
hydrogen_s1 <- load_cs(PATH_HYDROGEN_S1)
battery_s2  <- load_cs(PATH_BATTERY_S2)
hydrogen_s2 <- load_cs(PATH_HYDROGEN_S2)

# ROBUSTNESS = larger-control-group power spec (spec2: battery_s2, hydrogen_s2).
```

```{r outcome-map}
# ============================================================
# Outcome map: which column each technology uses.
# ============================================================
#
#   label                     battery column                 hydrogen column
#   ------------------------  -----------------------------  ------------------------------
#   technology-tagged (intens.)  log_collabs_battery         log_collabs_hydrogen

#   cross-sector              log_collabs_crosssector_battery     ..._hydrogen

#   non-EU (placebo)          log_collabs_non_eu_battery          ..._hydrogen
#   domestic (placebo)        log_collabs_domestic_battery        ..._hydrogen
#   within-sector (placebo)   log_collabs_withinsector_battery    ..._hydrogen
#   cross-sector (NACE-1)     log_collabs_crosssector_nace1_battery  ..._hydrogen  [robustness]
#
outcome_map <- list(
  tech_focused = c(battery = "log_collabs_battery",
                   hydrogen = "log_collabs_hydrogen"),
  cross_border = c(battery = "log_collabs_eu_crossborder_battery",
                   hydrogen = "log_collabs_eu_crossborder_hydrogen"),
  cross_sector = c(battery = "log_collabs_crosssector_battery",
                   hydrogen = "log_collabs_crosssector_hydrogen"),
  cross_sector_eu = c(battery = "log_collabs_crosssector_eu_battery",
                      hydrogen = "log_collabs_crosssector_eu_hydrogen"),
  non_eu = c(battery = "log_collabs_non_eu_battery",
             hydrogen = "log_collabs_non_eu_hydrogen"),
  domestic = c(battery = "log_collabs_domestic_battery",
               hydrogen = "log_collabs_domestic_hydrogen"),
  within_sector = c(battery = "log_collabs_withinsector_battery",
                    hydrogen = "log_collabs_withinsector_hydrogen"),
  # Redirection benchmark: collaboration OUTSIDE the funded technology
  # (total minus technology-tagged, built in nb03).
  non_funded    = c(battery = "log_collabs_nonfunded_battery",
                    hydrogen = "log_collabs_nonfunded_hydrogen"),
  # Robustness: cross-sector at NACE-1 resolution (nace2_proxy_nace1).
  # Same column auto-log-transformed by load_cs; primary cross_sector stays NACE-2.
  cross_sector_nace1 = c(battery = "log_collabs_crosssector_nace1_battery",
                         hydrogen = "log_collabs_crosssector_nace1_hydrogen")
)
```

```{r zero-shares}
# Zero shares among TREATED firm-periods (the binding constraint on power).
# Watch this when you flip to quarterly: it should drop noticeably.
zero_share_report <- function(df_b, df_h, map) {
  rows <- lapply(names(map), function(k) {
    cb <- sub("^log_collabs", "n_collabs", map[[k]]["battery"])
    ch <- sub("^log_collabs", "n_collabs", map[[k]]["hydrogen"])
    zb <- if (cb %in% names(df_b)) mean(df_b[df_b$is_treated == 1, cb] == 0) else NA
    zh <- if (ch %in% names(df_h)) mean(df_h[df_h$is_treated == 1, ch] == 0) else NA
    data.frame(outcome = k,
               battery_zero_pct  = round(100 * zb, 1),
               hydrogen_zero_pct = round(100 * zh, 1))
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
cat("\n--- Zero shares (treated firm-", TIME_UNIT, "s) ---\n", sep = "")
print(zero_share_report(battery_s1, hydrogen_s1, outcome_map), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 2. C&S Estimation --- Helper Functions

```{r cs-function}
run_cs <- function(df, yname, label = "",
                   control_group = "notyettreated",
                   clustervars   = NULL) {
  cat("\n=== C&S:", label, "(", yname, ") ===\n")
  if (!yname %in% names(df)) {
    cat("  !! column", yname, "not found -- skipping\n"); return(NULL)
  }
  # Deterministic per-outcome seed: makes every estimate reproducible and
  # independent of how many other outcomes ran earlier in the same session.
  # With a single set.seed() up front, adding one outcome shifts the bootstrap
  # stream for every later run and moves all downstream p-values.
  set.seed(42L + sum(utf8ToInt(paste0(yname, control_group))))
  cs_out <- att_gt(
    yname = yname, tname = "period", idname = "firm_id", gname = "g_period",
    control_group = control_group, clustervars = clustervars,
    anticipation = 0,   # paper assumption: treatment date = EC approval, no anticipation
    bstrap = TRUE, biters = BITERS, panel = TRUE, pl = TRUE, data = df
  )
  print(summary(cs_out))
  cs_out
}

agg_simple  <- function(cs) if (is.null(cs)) NULL else aggte(cs, type = "simple")
agg_dynamic <- function(cs) if (is.null(cs)) NULL else
  aggte(cs, type = "dynamic", min_e = -12, max_e = 24)

pval_from_att <- function(att, se) round(2 * pnorm(-abs(att / se)), 3)

sample_stats <- function(df, yname) {
  d <- df %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[yname]]), !is.na(firm_id),
                     !is.na(period), !is.na(g_period))
  data.frame(N_obs = nrow(d), N_units = n_distinct(d$firm_id),
             N_treated = n_distinct(d$firm_id[d$g_period > 0]))
}

# Pre-trend test. Primary is did's universal Wald pre-test (cs_out$Wpval). For
# staggered designs that bootstrap covariance is singular and att_gt returns no
# Wald (hydrogen, confirmed -- it stays NULL under never- AND not-yet-treated).
# In that case fall back to a joint test that the pre-period (e < 0) dynamic
# event-study coefficients are zero: a chi-square of their t-statistics from
# aggte(type="dynamic") att.egt/se.egt (analytic SEs, df = # pre-periods). The
# `method` field records which test was used.
es_pretrend <- function(cs_out) {
  if (is.null(cs_out)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  if (!is.null(cs_out$Wpval))
    return(list(stat = round(cs_out$W, 3), p = round(cs_out$Wpval, 3), method = "Wald"))
  dyn <- tryCatch(
    aggte(cs_out, type = "dynamic", min_e = -12, max_e = 24, bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(dyn)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  pre <- dyn$egt < 0
  t2  <- (dyn$att.egt[pre] / dyn$se.egt[pre])^2
  ok  <- is.finite(t2); k <- sum(ok)
  if (k == 0) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  stat <- sum(t2[ok])
  list(stat = round(stat, 3), p = round(1 - pchisq(stat, df = k), 3), method = "ES-joint")
}

make_att_row <- function(agg_obj, technology, outcome, type = "Primary",
                         cs_out = NULL, df = NULL, yname = NULL) {
  if (is.null(agg_obj)) return(NULL)
  stats <- if (!is.null(df) && !is.null(yname)) sample_stats(df, yname) else
    data.frame(N_obs = NA, N_units = NA, N_treated = NA)
  pt <- es_pretrend(cs_out)
  data.frame(
    Technology = technology, Outcome = outcome, Type = type,
    TimeUnit   = TIME_UNIT,
    ATT = round(agg_obj$overall.att, 4),
    SE  = round(agg_obj$overall.se, 4),
    p_value = pval_from_att(agg_obj$overall.att, agg_obj$overall.se),
    pretrend_stat    = pt$stat,
    pretrend_p_value = pt$p,
    pretrend_test    = pt$method,
    N_obs = stats$N_obs, N_units = stats$N_units, N_treated = stats$N_treated,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

plot_cs <- function(agg_dyn, title) {
  if (is.null(agg_dyn)) return(NULL)
  ggdid(agg_dyn, title = title) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    labs(x = paste0(toupper(substring(TIME_UNIT, 1, 1)),
                    substring(TIME_UNIT, 2), "s relative to treatment"),
         y = "ATT(g,t)")
}

# Primary C&S control group: NEVER-TREATED for BOTH technologies. Some firms are
# treated in multiple IPCEI rounds, so a not-yet-treated firm may already be
# affected by an earlier treatment and contaminate the control pool; never-treated
# controls avoid this and make the two technologies symmetric. (Battery is a
# single cohort, which independently requires never-treated.) The not-yet-treated
# alternative is reported as one robustness row for hydrogen (section 6).
cg_for <- function(technology) "nevertreated"

# Convenience: run battery + hydrogen for one outcome key from outcome_map.
# Primary spec: never-treated controls + firm-level clustering, both technologies.
run_pair <- function(key, label) {
  list(
    battery  = run_cs(battery_s1,  outcome_map[[key]]["battery"],
                      paste("Battery S2 --", label),
                      control_group = cg_for("battery"),
                      clustervars   = "firm_id"),
    hydrogen = run_cs(hydrogen_s1, outcome_map[[key]]["hydrogen"],
                      paste("Hydrogen S2 --", label),
                      control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"),
                      clustervars   = "firm_id")
  )
}
```

# 4. Summary Table

```{r summary-table}
spec <- list(
  list(cs_tech, "Technology-tagged collaborations", "Primary", "tech_focused"),
  list(cs_cb,   "Cross-border EU collaborations",    "Primary", "cross_border"),
  list(cs_xs,   "Cross-sector collaborations",       "Primary", "cross_sector"),
  list(cs_xs_n1,"Cross-sector collaborations (NACE-1)","Robustness (NACE-1)","cross_sector_nace1"),
  list(cs_neu,  "Non-EU collaborations",             "Placebo",    "non_eu"),
  list(cs_dom,  "Domestic collaborations",           "Placebo",    "domestic"),
  list(cs_ws,   "Within-sector collaborations",      "Placebo",    "within_sector"),
  list(cs_nf,   "Non-funded collaborations",         "Benchmark",  "non_funded"),
  list(cs_xseu, "Cross-sector EU-only collaborations","Primary","cross_sector_eu")
)

att_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(spec, function(s) {
  cs <- s[[1]]; outcome <- s[[2]]; type <- s[[3]]; key <- s[[4]]
  rbind(
    make_att_row(agg_simple(cs$battery), "Battery", outcome, type,
                 cs$battery, battery_s1, outcome_map[[key]]["battery"]),
    make_att_row(agg_simple(cs$hydrogen), "Hydrogen", outcome, type,
                 cs$hydrogen, hydrogen_s1, outcome_map[[key]]["hydrogen"])
  )
}))

cat("\n=== Tech-tagged ATT Summary (", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(att_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(att_table,
          file.path(out_dir, "att_techtagged_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r export-event-studies}
# ============================================================
# Export tech-tagged dynamic ATT(e) in long format for notebook 08.
# The es_*.pdf files are ggdid's default style; 08 redraws in house
# style from THIS csv. One row per (technology, outcome, event_time).
# ============================================================

# (technology, outcome-label, cs object) for every outcome we want an ES for.
# Labels MUST match the convention notebook 08 filters on. Adjust the label
# strings here if 08 expects a different separator/spelling.
es_spec <- list(
  list("Battery",  "Technology-tagged collaborations", cs_tech$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Technology-tagged collaborations", cs_tech$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Cross-border EU collaborations",   cs_cb$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Cross-border EU collaborations",   cs_cb$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Cross-sector collaborations",      cs_xs$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Cross-sector collaborations",      cs_xs$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Non-EU collaborations",            cs_neu$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Non-EU collaborations",            cs_neu$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Domestic collaborations",          cs_dom$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Domestic collaborations",          cs_dom$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Within-sector collaborations",     cs_ws$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Within-sector collaborations",     cs_ws$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Non-funded collaborations",        cs_nf$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Non-funded collaborations",        cs_nf$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Cross-sector EU-only collaborations", cs_xseu$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Cross-sector EU-only collaborations", cs_xseu$hydrogen)
)

# Consortium-size mechanism path: compute its C&S objects HERE so the dynamic
# event study is always exported. Section 10 (which writes consortium_size_att.csv)
# runs AFTER this chunk, so its cs_size does not yet exist on knit -- the old
# guard on exists("cs_size") silently dropped these rows. Estimator is IDENTICAL
# to Section 10: cg_for() control group, no clustering, so the ES matches the ATT.
# Event study uses the ACTIVE-month version (intensive margin), matching the
# headline mechanism in Section 10; falls back to the zero-filled column on old
# panels that predate 05a adding mean_collab_size_active.
SIZE_ES_COL <- if ("mean_collab_size_active" %in% names(battery_s1))
  "mean_collab_size_active" else "mean_collab_size"

if (RUN_CONSORTIUM && "mean_collab_size" %in% names(battery_s1)) {
  cs_size <- list(
    battery  = run_cs(battery_s1,  SIZE_ES_COL,
                      "Battery -- consortium size (mechanism)",
                      control_group = cg_for("battery")),
    hydrogen = run_cs(hydrogen_s1, SIZE_ES_COL,
                      "Hydrogen -- consortium size (mechanism)",
                      control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"))
  )
  es_spec <- c(es_spec, list(
    list("Battery",  "Consortium size (mean firms/collab)", cs_size$battery),
    list("Hydrogen", "Consortium size (mean firms/collab)", cs_size$hydrogen)
  ))
}

es_to_df <- function(tech, outcome, cs_obj) {
  if (is.null(cs_obj)) return(NULL)
  d <- tryCatch(agg_dynamic(cs_obj), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
  # Simultaneous band: aggte() is called with cband = TRUE, so crit.val.egt is
  # the uniform critical value over the whole event-time path. Falls back to the
  # pointwise normal value only if the bootstrap did not return one.
  z <- if (!is.null(d$crit.val.egt) && is.finite(d$crit.val.egt))
    d$crit.val.egt else qnorm(0.975)
  data.frame(
    label      = paste(tech, "--", outcome),   # match 08's label convention
    Technology = tech,
    Outcome    = outcome,
    e          = d$egt,
    att        = d$att.egt,
    se         = d$se.egt,
    crit_val   = z,
    ci_lower   = d$att.egt - z * d$se.egt,
    ci_upper   = d$att.egt + z * d$se.egt,
    TimeUnit   = TIME_UNIT,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

event_study_tt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(es_spec, function(s)
  es_to_df(s[[1]], s[[2]], s[[3]])))

write.csv(event_study_tt,
          file.path(out_dir, "event_study_techtagged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nWrote event_study_techtagged.csv:", nrow(event_study_tt), "rows,",
    length(unique(event_study_tt$label)), "outcome-technology series\n")
print(table(event_study_tt$label))
```

# 5. Extensive-margin robustness (binary outcome)

When a tech-tagged count is mostly zeros, a `log1p` ATT is dominated by the
zero mass and its magnitude is hard to read as an elasticity (Chen & Roth on
logs-with-zeros). A linear-probability C&S on the binary "any such tie this
period" outcome is an honest complement: the ATT is then a change in the
probability of forming that type of tie. Same identification, more
interpretable when events are rare.

```{r extensive-margin}
any_map <- lapply(outcome_map, function(v) sub("^log_collabs", "any_collabs", v))

ext_keys <- c("tech_focused", "cross_border", "cross_sector")  # the ones we care about
ext_rows <- list()
for (key in ext_keys) {
  cb <- run_cs(battery_s1,  any_map[[key]]["battery"],
               paste("Battery S2 -- EXT", key),
               control_group = cg_for("battery"))   # single cohort -> nevertreated
  ch <- run_cs(hydrogen_s1, any_map[[key]]["hydrogen"],
               paste("Hydrogen S2 -- EXT", key),
               control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"))
  ext_rows[[length(ext_rows) + 1]] <-
    make_att_row(agg_simple(cb), "Battery", paste0("[ext] ", key), "Ext. margin",
                 cb, battery_s1, any_map[[key]]["battery"])
  ext_rows[[length(ext_rows) + 1]] <-
    make_att_row(agg_simple(ch), "Hydrogen", paste0("[ext] ", key), "Ext. margin",
                 ch, hydrogen_s1, any_map[[key]]["hydrogen"])
}
ext_table <- do.call(rbind, ext_rows)
cat("\n=== Extensive-margin ATT (", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(ext_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ext_table,
          file.path(out_dir, "att_extensive_margin.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 6. Robustness (technology-tagged)

The primary spec (section 4) is the tighter-balance matched sample (`battery_s1`
= 1:3, `hydrogen_s1` = cal20_r2) with never-treated controls + firm-level
clustering. Robustness reuses `run_cs()` + `outcome_map`, the contiguous period
index and the firm-quarter aggregation (inheriting the `TIME_UNIT` toggle) and
reports two checks: (a) **larger control group** -- the SAME never-treated +
firm-clustered estimator re-run on the higher-ratio power matched sample
(`battery_s2` = 1:7, `hydrogen_s2` = cal15_r3); and (b)
**not-yet-treated controls** as one shown alternative (hydrogen only -- battery
is a single cohort with no not-yet-treated units), so the reader sees the primary
never-treated choice does not drive the results. The table is parallel to
section 4.

```{r robustness-techtagged}
# Outcomes to re-run -- mirrors the section-4 spec list (the optional
# cross_sector_eu outcome is skipped here).
rob_spec <- list(
  list("tech_focused",  "Technology-tagged collaborations"),
  list("cross_border",  "Cross-border EU collaborations"),
  list("cross_sector",  "Cross-sector collaborations"),
  list("cross_sector_nace1", "Cross-sector collaborations (NACE-1)"),
  list("non_eu",        "Non-EU collaborations"),
  list("domestic",      "Domestic collaborations"),
  list("within_sector", "Within-sector collaborations"),
  list("non_funded",    "Non-funded collaborations")
)

# One robustness ATT row: pick the tech-tagged column from outcome_map, run C&S
# with the requested variant, return a section-4-parallel row (NULL-safe).
rob_one <- function(df, key, technology, outcome, variant,
                    control_group = NULL, clustervars = NULL) {
  # Default to the primary control group (never-treated, via cg_for). The
  # "Not-yet-treated controls" variant passes control_group explicitly to override.
  if (is.null(control_group)) control_group <- cg_for(technology)
  yn <- outcome_map[[key]][tolower(technology)]
  cs <- run_cs(df, yn,
               label         = paste(technology, "--", outcome, "--", variant),
               control_group = control_group,
               clustervars   = clustervars)
  make_att_row(agg_simple(cs), technology, outcome, variant, cs, df, yn)
}

rob_rows <- list()
for (s in rob_spec) {
  key <- s[[1]]; oc <- s[[2]]
  rob_rows <- c(rob_rows, list(
    # (a) larger control group (power spec, S2): SAME primary estimator
    #     (never-treated + firm clustering) on the higher-ratio matched sample
    rob_one(battery_s2,  key, "Battery",  oc, "Larger control group", clustervars = "firm_id"),
    rob_one(hydrogen_s2, key, "Hydrogen", oc, "Larger control group", clustervars = "firm_id"),
    # (b) not-yet-treated controls (hydrogen only; battery is a single cohort with
    #     no not-yet-treated units) -- shows the never-treated primary choice does
    #     not drive results
    rob_one(hydrogen_s1, key, "Hydrogen", oc, "Not-yet-treated controls",
            control_group = "notyettreated", clustervars = "firm_id")
  ))
}
rob_table <- do.call(rbind, rob_rows)

cat("\n=== Robustness checks (tech-tagged,", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(rob_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(rob_table,
          file.path(out_dir, "robustness_techtagged_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 7. Rosenbaum Bounds (technology-tagged)

Method preserved exactly from the original file: collapse each matched set to a
post-treatment pair difference (treated firm vs the mean of its matched
controls, on `log1p` of the count) and run a Wilcoxon signed-rank sensitivity
analysis with `rbounds::psens` / `hlsens`. It reads the matched-firms and
cs_ready CSVs directly and works off the raw `month` / `g` dates, so it is a
matched-pair analysis unaffected by the period coding; only the tech-tagged
**count** columns (`n_collabs_*`, not the logs) are fed in. Outputs go to the
`TIME_UNIT` results folder.

```{r rosenbaum-function}
run_rosenbaum <- function(matched_firms_path, cs_panel_path,
                           outcome_col = "n_collabs_battery",
                           gamma_max   = 3.0,
                           gamma_inc   = 0.1,
                           label       = "") {

  cat("\n=== Rosenbaum Bounds:", label, "===\n")

  firms <- read.csv(matched_firms_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  panel <- read.csv(cs_panel_path,      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  panel$month <- as.Date(panel$month)

  g_lookup <- panel %>%
    filter(is_treated == 1) %>%
    distinct(Linkedin_name, matched_to, g) %>%
    rename(g_treated = g)

  panel_sym <- panel %>%
    left_join(
      g_lookup %>% select(matched_to, g_treated),
      by = "matched_to"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      g_use  = ifelse(is_treated == 1, g, g_treated),
      g_date = as.Date(g_use),
      post   = !is.na(g_date) & month >= g_date
    ) %>%
    mutate(y = log1p(.data[[outcome_col]])) %>%
    group_by(Linkedin_name) %>%
    # DiD contrast, not a post-treatment level: each firm's own post-minus-pre
    # change. Pairing these changes makes the Rosenbaum null correspond to the
    # difference-in-differences estimand rather than to a level difference.
    summarise(y_mean = mean(y[post], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(y[!post], na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(is.finite(y_mean))

  firms <- firms %>%
    left_join(panel_sym, by = "Linkedin_name")

  treated <- firms %>%
    filter(is_treated == 1) %>%
    select(matched_to, Linkedin_name, y_treated = y_mean) %>%
    rename(treated_name = Linkedin_name)

  controls_agg <- firms %>%
    filter(is_control == 1) %>%
    group_by(matched_to) %>%
    summarise(y_control = mean(y_mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  pairs <- treated %>%
    left_join(controls_agg, by = "matched_to") %>%
    filter(!is.na(y_treated), !is.na(y_control))

  cat(sprintf("  Valid matched pairs: %d\n", nrow(pairs)))
  cat(sprintf("  Mean treated: %.3f | Mean control: %.3f\n",
              mean(pairs$y_treated), mean(pairs$y_control)))

  cat("\n-- Wilcoxon signed-rank sensitivity (psens) --\n")
  ps <- psens(pairs$y_treated, pairs$y_control,
              Gamma = gamma_max, GammaInc = gamma_inc)

  cat("\n-- Hodges-Lehmann sensitivity (hlsens) --\n")
  hl <- hlsens(pairs$y_treated, pairs$y_control,
               Gamma = gamma_max, GammaInc = gamma_inc)

  psens_df    <- as.data.frame(ps$bounds)
  gamma_break <- psens_df$Gamma[which(psens_df$`Lower Bound` > 0.05)[1]]

  cat(sprintf("\n  Lower bound p at Gamma=1: %.4f\n",
              psens_df$`Lower Bound`[1]))
  cat(sprintf("  Effect robust to hidden bias up to Gamma = %.1f\n",
              ifelse(is.na(gamma_break), gamma_max, gamma_break - gamma_inc)))

  invisible(list(psens = ps, hlsens = hl,
                 gamma_break = gamma_break, pairs = pairs))
}
```

```{r rosenbaum-run, eval=RUN_ROSENBAUM}
# Dynamic selection: test exactly the outcomes that are significant in THIS run
# (same derivation as the section-9 power sim), using the global SIG_THRESHOLD
# from the setup chunk. key_by_outcome is defined here too (same values).
key_by_outcome <- c(
  "Technology-tagged collaborations"    = "tech_focused",
  "Cross-border EU collaborations"      = "cross_border",
  "Cross-sector collaborations"         = "cross_sector",
  "Cross-sector EU-only collaborations" = "cross_sector_eu",
  "Non-EU collaborations"               = "non_eu",
  "Domestic collaborations"             = "domestic",
  "Within-sector collaborations"        = "within_sector",
  "Non-funded collaborations"           = "non_funded"
)

sig_rb <- att_table[!is.na(att_table$p_value) &
                      att_table$p_value < SIG_THRESHOLD, , drop = FALSE]
sig_rb$key <- key_by_outcome[sig_rb$Outcome]
sig_rb <- sig_rb[!is.na(sig_rb$key), , drop = FALSE]

# Feed the tech-tagged COUNT column (n_collabs_*, not the log) for each
# significant (Technology, outcome) pair; matched-pair method unchanged.
if (nrow(sig_rb) == 0) {
  cat("No significant outcomes (p <", SIG_THRESHOLD,
      ") -- Rosenbaum bounds skipped.\n")
  rb_runs <- list()
} else {
  rb_runs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sig_rb)), function(i) {
    tech  <- sig_rb$Technology[i]
    is_b  <- tech == "Battery"
    fpath <- if (is_b) PATH_BATTERY_FIRMS_S1 else PATH_HYDROGEN_FIRMS_S1
    ppath <- if (is_b) PATH_BATTERY_S1       else PATH_HYDROGEN_S1
    ccol  <- sub("^log_collabs", "n_collabs",
                 outcome_map[[sig_rb$key[i]]][tolower(tech)])
    run_rosenbaum(fpath, ppath, outcome_col = ccol,
                  label = paste(tech, "--", sig_rb$Outcome[i]))
  })
  names(rb_runs) <- paste(sig_rb$Technology, "--", sig_rb$Outcome)
}
```

```{r rosenbaum-table, eval=RUN_ROSENBAUM}
if (length(rb_runs) == 0) {
  cat("Rosenbaum bounds table skipped (no significant outcomes).\n")
} else {
  make_rb_table <- function(rb_obj, label) {
    df <- as.data.frame(rb_obj$psens$bounds)
    df$Specification <- label
    df %>% select(Specification, everything())
  }

  rb_table <- bind_rows(Map(make_rb_table, rb_runs, names(rb_runs))) %>%
    filter(Gamma %in% c(1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0))

  cat("\n=== Rosenbaum bounds (tech-tagged,", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
  print(rb_table, row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(rb_table,
            file.path(out_dir, "rosenbaum_bounds_techtagged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# 8. Benjamini--Hochberg Correction (technology-tagged)

BH applied **within each value chain**, across that chain's outcomes, using the
p-values from the section-4 `att_table` (computed under the current
`TIME_UNIT`).

```{r bh-correction}
bh_stars <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "",
                        ifelse(p < 0.01, "***",
                        ifelse(p < 0.05, "**",
                        ifelse(p < 0.10, "*", ""))))

make_bh_df <- function(tech) {
  sub   <- att_table[att_table$Technology == tech, ]
  p_raw <- sub$p_value
  p_bh  <- p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH")
  data.frame(
    technology = tech,
    outcome    = sub$Outcome,
    p_raw      = round(p_raw, 3),
    p_bh       = round(p_bh,  3),
    sig_raw    = bh_stars(p_raw),
    sig_bh     = bh_stars(p_bh),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

bh_df <- rbind(make_bh_df("Battery"), make_bh_df("Hydrogen"))

cat("\n=== Benjamini-Hochberg (per value chain,", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(bh_df, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(bh_df,
          file.path(out_dir, "bh_correction_techtagged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 9. Power Simulation (dynamic --- significant outcomes only)

Design-based power simulation ported verbatim from the original file: synthetic
treated firms are drawn from the matched controls reproducing the real cohort
sizes, a constant additive effect is imposed on the log outcome over the
post-period, the C&S overall ATT is re-estimated per draw, and the rejection
rate at the 5% level is recorded. The methodology and the per-effect-size draw
count are unchanged. The only change: it runs **only on the outcomes flagged as
findings** in section 4 (`p_value < SIG_THRESHOLD`), mapped back to their
`outcome_map` keys, and the combined plot shows just those, each with a
vertical line at its estimated ATT.

```{r power-function}
run_power_sim <- function(cs_data, outcome_var, att_true,
                          n_sims = 100, label = "") {
  controls_df   <- cs_data[cs_data$is_control == 1, ]
  control_names <- unique(controls_df$Linkedin_name)

  real_cohorts <- cs_data %>%
    filter(is_treated == 1) %>%
    distinct(Linkedin_name, g_period) %>%
    count(g_period) %>%
    arrange(g_period)

  results <- numeric(n_sims)

  for (i in seq_len(n_sims)) {
    available    <- control_names
    treated_pool <- character(0)
    g_vec        <- integer(0)

    for (k in seq_len(nrow(real_cohorts))) {
      n_k    <- real_cohorts$n[k]
      cohort <- real_cohorts$g_period[k]
      if (length(available) < n_k) break
      sampled      <- sample(available, n_k, replace = FALSE)
      available    <- setdiff(available, sampled)
      treated_pool <- c(treated_pool, sampled)
      g_vec        <- c(g_vec, rep(cohort, n_k))
    }

    g_lookup <- data.frame(Linkedin_name = treated_pool,
                           g_sim = g_vec,
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

    sim_treated <- controls_df %>%
      filter(Linkedin_name %in% treated_pool) %>%
      left_join(g_lookup, by = "Linkedin_name") %>%
      mutate(post_sim     = as.integer(period >= g_sim),
             outcome_sim  = .data[[outcome_var]] + att_true * post_sim,
             g_period_sim = g_sim)

    sim_controls <- controls_df %>%
      filter(Linkedin_name %in% available) %>%
      mutate(outcome_sim  = .data[[outcome_var]],
             g_period_sim = 0L)

    sim_data <- bind_rows(sim_treated, sim_controls) %>%
      mutate(firm_id_sim = as.integer(factor(Linkedin_name)))

    result <- tryCatch({
      cs_sim <- att_gt(
        yname         = "outcome_sim",
        tname         = "period",
        idname        = "firm_id_sim",
        gname         = "g_period_sim",
        control_group = "notyettreated",
        anticipation  = 0,   # paper assumption: no anticipation
        bstrap        = FALSE,
        panel         = TRUE,
        print_details = FALSE,
        data          = sim_data
      )
      agg_sim <- aggte(cs_sim, type = "simple")
      z_stat  <- agg_sim$overall.att / agg_sim$overall.se
      as.integer(abs(z_stat) > 1.96)
    }, error = function(e) NA_integer_)

    results[i] <- result
  }

  mean(results, na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

```{r power-sig-set}

# Map section-4 display names back to outcome_map keys.
# (SIG_THRESHOLD comes from the setup chunk.)
key_by_outcome <- c(
  "Technology-tagged collaborations"    = "tech_focused",
  "Cross-border EU collaborations"      = "cross_border",
  "Cross-sector collaborations"         = "cross_sector",
  "Cross-sector EU-only collaborations" = "cross_sector_eu",
  "Non-EU collaborations"               = "non_eu",
  "Domestic collaborations"             = "domestic",
  "Within-sector collaborations"        = "within_sector",
  "Non-funded collaborations"           = "non_funded"
)

sig_rows <- att_table[!is.na(att_table$p_value) &
                        att_table$p_value < SIG_THRESHOLD, , drop = FALSE]
sig_rows$key <- key_by_outcome[sig_rows$Outcome]
sig_rows <- sig_rows[!is.na(sig_rows$key), , drop = FALSE]

if (nrow(sig_rows) == 0) {

        row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r power-run, eval=RUN_POWER}
library(parallel)

# Robust parallelism: fork when available, but fall back to serial if the fork
# workers fail (e.g. a non-interactive session), so an overnight run never
# silently returns no results. Shadows parallel::mclapply for the calls below.
mclapply <- function(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = min(4L, parallel::detectCores())) {
  res <- tryCatch(parallel::mclapply(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = mc.cores),
                  error = function(e) base::lapply(X, FUN))
  if (any(vapply(res, function(z) inherits(z, "try-error"), logical(1))))
    res <- base::lapply(X, FUN)
  res
}

att_grid     <- log(1 + c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30))
att_pct_grid <- round((exp(att_grid) - 1) * 100, 1)

if (nrow(sig_rows) == 0) {
  cat("No significant outcomes -- skipping power simulation.\n")
  power_long <- NULL
} else {
  power_rows <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(sig_rows))) {
    tech  <- sig_rows$Technology[i]
    key   <- sig_rows$key[i]
    oc    <- sig_rows$Outcome[i]
    dfp   <- if (tech == "Battery") battery_s1 else hydrogen_s1
    yname <- outcome_map[[key]][tolower(tech)]
    lbl   <- paste(tech, "--", oc)

    cat("Power simulation:", lbl, "(", yname, ")\n")
    pw <- unlist(mclapply(att_grid, function(a)
      run_power_sim(dfp, yname, a, 100, lbl), mc.cores = 4))

    power_rows[[length(power_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      spec    = lbl,
      att_pct = att_pct_grid,
      power   = pw,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
  power_long <- do.call(rbind, power_rows)
  print(power_long)
  write.csv(power_long,
            file.path(out_dir, "power_techtagged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r power-plot, eval=RUN_POWER}
if (!is.null(power_long)) {
  power_long$Technology <- sub(" --.*$", "", power_long$spec)
  power_long$Technology <- paste(power_long$Technology, "IPCEI")
  power_long$Outcome    <- sub("^.* -- ", "", power_long$spec)

  # Annex figure defends the SIGNIFICANT results -> keep only those.
  # (No-op if the power sim already ran on sig_rows only.)
  sig_specs  <- paste(sig_rows$Technology, "--", sig_rows$Outcome)
  power_long <- power_long[power_long$spec %in% sig_specs, ]

  vlines <- data.frame(

  out_lvls <- sort(unique(power_long$Outcome))
  out_cols <- setNames(

  p_power <- ggplot(power_long,

    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ Technology) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = out_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0.6, 1),

    labs(x = "True treatment effect (% change in outcome)",
         y = "Simulated power", colour = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 8),
          panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"),
          strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold"))
  print(p_power)
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "power_techtagged_plot.pdf"),
         p_power, width = 9, height = 5)
} else {
  cat("Power plot skipped (no significant outcomes).\n")
}
```

# 10. Consortium size (mechanism check)

Did treated firms join LARGER multi-firm collaborations after approval? This is a
potential mechanical driver of the composition results. `mean_collab_size` is the
mean number of firms per collaboration a firm participates in, per period --- a
**level**, not a count and not a share. It is run on the RAW column: no `log1p`,
not in `outcome_map`. Technology-specific control group via `cg_for()`
(battery `nevertreated`, hydrogen `notyettreated`); `anticipation = 0` is already
set inside `run_cs()`. `TIME_UNIT`-aware (quarterly averages the per-month means).

```{r consortium-size}
# Two versions, see the note above:
#   mean_collab_size_active -- NA in firm-months without a collaboration, so C&S
#     drops them and the ATT is INTENSIVE margin. This is the headline mechanism.
#   mean_collab_size        -- zero-filled, mixes extensive and intensive margins.
#     Reported alongside so the difference between the two is visible.
SIZE_COLS <- c(active = "mean_collab_size_active", allmonths = "mean_collab_size")
SIZE_LAB  <- c(active = "Consortium size (active months)",
               allmonths = "Consortium size (incl. zero-collaboration months)")

if (RUN_CONSORTIUM && "mean_collab_size" %in% names(battery_s1)) {
  cs_size <- list(); size_rows <- list()
  for (v in names(SIZE_COLS)) {
    col <- SIZE_COLS[[v]]
    if (!(col %in% names(battery_s1))) {
      cat("   ", col, "not in panel -- re-run 05a. Skipping.\n"); next
    }
    cs_size[[v]] <- list(
      battery  = run_cs(battery_s1,  col,
                        paste("Battery --", SIZE_LAB[[v]]),
                        control_group = cg_for("battery")),
      hydrogen = run_cs(hydrogen_s1, col,
                        paste("Hydrogen --", SIZE_LAB[[v]]),
                        control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"))
    )
    size_rows[[v]] <- do.call(rbind, list(
      make_att_row(agg_simple(cs_size[[v]]$battery),  "Battery",
                   SIZE_LAB[[v]], "Mechanism",
                   cs_size[[v]]$battery,  battery_s1,  col),
      make_att_row(agg_simple(cs_size[[v]]$hydrogen), "Hydrogen",
                   SIZE_LAB[[v]], "Mechanism",
                   cs_size[[v]]$hydrogen, hydrogen_s1, col)
    ))
  }
  size_table <- do.call(rbind, size_rows)
  # Back-compat: downstream code expects cs_size$battery / cs_size$hydrogen.
  cs_size <- if (!is.null(cs_size$active)) cs_size$active else cs_size$allmonths
  cat("\n=== Consortium size mechanism check (", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
  print(size_table, row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(size_table,
            file.path(out_dir, "consortium_size_att.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("mean_collab_size not found in cs_ready panels --",
      "re-run notebook 05 to add it. Skipping mechanism check.\n")
}
```
